transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-05-06
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Diaz (Redwood SE), Jared Kim (AtlasPay ML), Priya Rao (AtlasPay Infra), Ahmed El-Sayed (AtlasPay DS), Sofia Martinez (AtlasPay SRE), Liam O'Connor (AtlasPay Product)

Summary: quick weekly sync on INT8 / FP8 quantization experiments. Reviewed perf deltas, quality impact on eval sets, infra considerations for dedicated benchmark, and next steps for A/B test + security docs. Some transcription artifacts present. Referenced artifacts: quant-report-v3.pdf, perf-spreadsheet.xlsx (Drive link).

Topics: [results review, tuning notes, infra & security, next steps]

Transcript: 
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): all right everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick check-in for the quant experiments, we got about 45 minutes, we'll run through results and then next steps.
[00:18] Jared (AtlasPay): sounds good, Maya. sorry fam a bit behind but ready.
[00:22] Carlos (Redwood SE): no worries. i posted the perf spreadsheet in the drive link earlier, quant-report-v3.pdf, and there's a short summary slide.
[00:30] Priya (AtlasPay Infra): we got the cluster window next week for the dedicated run, just need the exact instance sizes.
[00:38] Maya: perfect. ok Carlos, can you walk through the headline numbers first?
[00:42] Carlos: yeah. so baseline was FP16 on our standard v4-like instance (NVIDIA A100 equiv), throughput ~140 tokens/sec for the 2k context eval. INT8 gave us ~260 tokens/sec in our test bed, so roughly a 1.85x throughput uplift. FP8 experiments (experimental) showed ~320 tokens/sec, so ~2.3x. latency P95 improved from 420ms down to 270ms on INT8, and to ~230ms with FP8 in our harness. caveat: these are microbenchmarks with synthetic load and no KV cache warm.
[01:20] Ahmed (AtlasPay DS): those numbers look great, what's the quality delta? we worry about hallucination/regression on our summarization flow.
[01:26] Carlos: good Q. we ran the 5k prompt eval set (mix of summarization, Q/A, rewrite). INT8 had a small drop: rouge-L decreased by ~0.8 points average, and exact-match for QA dropped ~0.6%. FP8 was slightly worse: rouge-L down ~1.6 and EM down ~1.4%. perplexity rose marginally: +0.9 for INT8, +1.9 for FP8. so quality impact is present but relatively small depending on metric sensitivity.
[02:08] Jared: on our fraud-detection generation, even a small EM delta can be material. do you have per-task breakdown?
[02:14] Carlos: yes, per task INT8 is almost negligible on classification-style outputs, larger on abstractive summarization. i'll upload the per-task sheets.
[02:22] Maya: important to highlight prompts where tokenization/formatting caused more regressions — some were prompt-length sensitive, the quantization bins interacted with layernorm in odd ways in FP8.
[02:32] Sofia (SRE): were these runs with KV cache enabled? we rely on long context for a lot of our traces.
[02:36] Carlos: KV cache was disabled for the bulk of perf tests to get steady-state generation numbers. we did a small subset with KV warm and saw slightly better latency improvements but throughput numbers are similar. we'll run dedicated KV warm benchmarks next week.
[02:50] Priya: for the dedicated cluster, what hardware do you recommend? we can book A100x2 or the H100 flavor, what's the Redwood guidance?
[02:56] Maya: for INT8/FP8 experiments we recommend H100-equivalent for FP8 performance — hardware-native FP8 paths are better — but INT8 runs well on A100 with quant kernels. cost trade-offs apply.
[03:10] Ahmed: can you explain the kernel variation? our infra folks want to know if we need to compile custom kernels or just use Redwood runtime.
[03:16] Carlos: so the runtime auto-selects kernels based on model arch and seq length; for INT8 we use quantized GEMM kernels and f16 accumulation, FP8 uses new FP8 kernels where available. Redwood runtime will auto-pick but we capture kernel selection logs if you want to see which path taken. for dedicated we can expose more verbose logs.
[03:40] Liam (Product): what about cost delta? rough numbers per 1M tokens?
[03:44] Maya: rough ballpark from our internal pricing model: INT8 reduces per-token GPU compute cost by ~40% vs FP16, FP8 about ~50%, but network and overheads reduce some of that for small requests. we'll send a model-specific cost table.
[03:58] Jared: i noticed some weird transcription here, a couple words look mis-typed in the report, we should rely on raw evals.
[04:03] Maya: agreed. the drive has the raw CSVs.
[04:08] Carlos: tuning notes: 1) mixed-precision fine tuning (PTQ with layerwise calibration) helped reduce rouge delta for INT8 by ~0.3 points. 2) per-channel clipping for weights on certain attention heads reduced spikes. 3) we saw more sensitivity in layers near the embeddings and the final norm, so we applied higher precision there as a hybrid approach (INT8 except some layers f16).
[04:44] Ahmed: hybrid is interesting — what's the perf hit?
[04:47] Carlos: hybrid reduced the throughput gain a bit, from 1.85x to ~1.6x for INT8-hybrid, but the rouge delta came down to ~0.2 points which may be acceptable.
[04:58] Priya: from infra, memory footprint numbers? if INT8 halves weight memory that helps more models fit per GPU.
[05:03] Carlos: yes, model weight memory dropped ~48% with INT8, FP8 ~60% in our packing. activation memory varies; with KV cache it still matters, but more models can be packed per node.
[05:18] Sofia: for Private deployment we need to confirm KMS and audit integrations. Maya, you said you'd share security docs?
[05:22] Maya: yes, sending SOC2/ISO summary and audit log samples, plus how KMS is used for key wrapping in private. Priya please confirm the KMS endpoint test account works.
[05:33] Priya: will do. also we need sample traffic shaping to not blow outage windows during dedicated run. what's Redwood's recommended schedule?
[05:40] Carlos: best to do a 4-hour window off-peak, run several sweeps: cold-starts, KV-warm, and sustained QPS. we'll provide exact scripts.
[05:50] Ahmed: any regressions on safety heuristics with quant? we're using a safety filter post-gen.
[05:54] Carlos: no significant changes observed in the safety classifier because that runs in post-processing; generative regressions are more content-quality than toxicity in our tests. still we'll run targeted safety prompts in the A/B.
[06:10] Jared: what's the plan for rollback if we see unacceptable deltas in production?
[06:14] Maya: Redwood provides model-variant routing fallback; you can route to FP16 baseline for a percentage of traffic and do canary. we can set auto-fallback if quality metrics cross thresholds.
[06:26] Liam: will Redwood instrument eval metrics into our console? so product can see per-route rouge/EM etc.
[06:31] Maya: yes, Redwood Console can surface per-route QA and custom evals if you feed back the eval harness results; we can wire it to your S3 bucket of evals.
[06:44] Carlos: quick note on prompt sensitivity — we saw certain templated prompts where integer quantization aggravated tokenization edge-cases; recommended to add prompt normalization in the client side for canary.
[06:58] Priya: what's the expected timeline to get a stable INT8 config?
[07:02] Carlos: with the hybrid tuning approach we can produce an INT8 config with sub-0.5 rouge drop in ~1-2 sprints; for your eval set i think 1 sprint (2 weeks) to run canaries and iterate.
[07:18] Maya: ok action items recap coming at the end. any blockers from AtlasPay?
[07:22] Jared: need the scripts and quant configs, and the dedicated window details. also want the per-prompt fail list.
[07:29] Maya: noted. Carlos will share the configs + per-prompt regression list.
[07:35] Carlos: i'll also attach kernel logs and raw perf traces. the perf spreadsheet includes full CSVs.
[07:41] Sophia (sic, Sofia): small nit — earlier you said drive link, can you post in the ticket as well? it's easier for infra.
[07:46] Maya: yes will post in the Jira ticket, also emailing.
[07:50] Carlos: quickly on FP8 risk: FP8 toolchain is still experimental across some vendors; we recommend production only with careful canarying and fallback. INT8 is safer for now.
[08:05] Ahmed: ok that aligns with our risk tolerance.
[08:07] Liam: product asks whether we should A/B INT8 vs FP16 or do AB with hybrid?
[08:12] Maya: start with INT8-hybrid vs FP16 baseline. that gives a good quality/throughput tradeoff. if INT8-pure looks good we can widen.
[08:23] Jared: timeline: we'll run 1k prompt A/B after configs arrive, target results by 2025-05-13.
[08:29] Maya: sounds good. Carlos — can you confirm you'll schedule the dedicated benchmark?
[08:33] Carlos: yes, i'll book for Tue 2025-05-13 morning PST, pending Priya's infra window confirmation.
[08:40] Priya: confirmed tentative slot, i'll lock and share VPC peering details.
[08:46] Maya: great. any other questions?
[08:49] Ahmed: one more — can Redwood provide a short explainer on how per-layer higher precision works so our models team can review?
[08:55] Carlos: yes i'll include a one-pager describing hybrid layer selection heuristics + config template.
[09:02] Maya: ok let's do recap.
[09:05] Maya: recap / next steps: 1) Maya share quant configs, perf spreadsheet, SOC2/ISO docs (due 5/9). 2) Carlos schedule dedicated benchmark (5/13) and attach kernel logs. 3) Jared run 1k prompt A/B (5/13) and return raw evals. 4) Priya validate KMS and VPC peering (5/12). 5) Team to agree stopping metric and threshold for auto-fallback.
[09:35] Jared: that's all from us, thanks.
[09:37] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in the ticket and send the package after the call.
[09:41] Meeting end.
